concept: Data Federation over customer S3 with partitioning
summary: Source-anchored research for Data Federation over customer S3 with partitioning. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Partition-key predicates are a general scan-control pattern across object-store query engines: AWS Athena describes pruning S3 partitions that do not match query predicates, and Trino's Hive connector documents dynamic partition pruning and an optional requirement for partition filters. These are cross-engine context and do not mean Athena or Trino settings apply to Atlas Data Federation. (medium confidence) Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/ctas-partitioning-and-bucketing-what-is-partitioning.html ; https://trino.io/docs/current/connector/hive.html

Data Federation adds partition attributes to documents even when a field with the same name already exists in the document, creating duplicate field names that MongoDB does not support. To avoid this, set `omitAttributes` to `true` or use partition attribute names that don't appear in your documents. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/data-federation/config/path-syntax-examples.md

Give path partition attributes names that do not collide with fields inside the documents. Atlas Data Federation adds partition attributes to documents even when a field with the same name already exists, which creates duplicate field names. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/data-federation/config/path-syntax-examples.md

Avoid layouts that create many small files or excessive partitions. MongoDB says many small files compound per-file resource use and large files can require unnecessary downloads; AWS Athena separately warns that too many S3 partitions add file and partition-filtering overhead, while too few can increase scans. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/data-federation/admin/optimize-query-performance.md ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/performance-tuning-data-optimization-techniques.html

Selective partition matches can reduce Data Federation's processed bytes and charges, but partitioning does not guarantee savings: a query that reads the whole collection still processes the whole collection. MongoDB's example contrasts reading one 1 GB partition from a 10 GB file layout with processing all 10 GB when no partition can be skipped. (high confidence)
MongoDB's billing page lists Data Federation processing at $5 per TB with a 10 MB minimum per query. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18)

MongoDB recommends ordering S3 partition fields from the most frequently queried to the least frequently queried. A query that skips an earlier path field can use matching earlier partitions more efficiently than later ones; fields absent from the configured path cannot prune files. (high confidence)

For customer-managed S3, a collection's `dataSources.path` can map S3 key segments to computed partition attributes, and Data Federation can target queries on those attributes to only the files with a matching file name or partition prefix. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/data-federation/config/path-syntax-examples.md

Atlas Data Federation maps configured S3 stores to virtual databases and collections. Its data-source path syntax can parse key or filename segments into typed partition attributes and add those attributes to query documents. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/data-federation/adf-overview/key-concepts/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/data-federation/config/path-syntax-examples.md

Atlas charges separately for data processed and data returned or transferred. A filter on mapped S3 path attributes can target matching files and reduce processed bytes, but a broad query such as a blank $match still reads the full collection, so partitioning alone does not guarantee lower processing cost. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/data-federation/query/query-federated-database.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/data-federation/config/path-syntax-examples.md
